title: Intro Python Quiz 3: strings and lists

questions.text: In count_vowels you stored the vowels in a set. Why did you choose a set instead of a list or a plain string?
questions.transcript: I used a set because I only need to check if a letter is a vowel. Membership checks in a set are fast and the order does not matter, though a list would also work for five letters.
questions.feedback: Covers fast membership checks and why order does not matter, and notes a list would also work.

questions.text: In remove_duplicates, walk me through what seen and result hold after the loop has processed the list 3, 1, 3, 2.
questions.transcript: After the loop seen holds 3, 1 and 2 and result is 3, 1, 2. The second three is skipped because it is already in seen.
questions.feedback: Traces both seen and result correctly and explains the skipped duplicate.

questions.text: Two of your tests failed when the list contained other lists, like [[1], [1]]. Why did that fail, and how could you change your code to handle it?
questions.transcript: Lists are not hashable so putting one in a set raises a TypeError. I could keep seen as a list or convert the inner lists to tuples first.
questions.feedback: Names unhashable lists and both fixes; does not say where the error is raised.
